_readme: GEAR CATALOG: the single source for every tradeable item. Edit this file, then run `node tools/gen_gear.js`.
The generator rewrites the GEN:BEGIN/GEN:END blocks in the scenes, inventory-data.js and startup.txt.
Never edit inside a generated block by hand: the next run overwrites it.
Item fields:
id        internal id; the ownership flag is always has_<id> (set create:false if hand-created elsewhere)
kind      armor | shield | weapon | head | cloak | hands | waist | feet | neck | tool | ring | consumable | salvage | valuable
tradeGroup OPTIONAL finer trade-panel category for items sharing a kind (currently jewelry; valuables otherwise appear as loose stones)
name      short lower-case noun used in menus and shop prose ('mail shirt')
(the equipment slot an item fills, such as Cloak, Hands or Body armor, is derived from `kind` by gen_gear.js
slotLabel and shown in the shop menus, the trade panel and the inventory; tools and consumables show none)
title     proper display name used by the dossier and the inventory panel. Keep it to THREE WORDS OR FEWER (a longer
title wraps to a second line in the panels) and leave treatment words (boiled, oiled, waxed, tarred, riveted,
lined) and lore out of it: put those in `blurb` and the dossier `line` ('Leather Watch Cap', not
'Boiled-Hide Watch Cap'). `name` is the lower-case noun for menu sentences and follows the same rule.
retail    shop price in copper (10 copper = 1 silver)
minutes   how long a fitting or handover takes when bought
hint      the [stat hint] shown on a buy option when the player has hints on
blurb     one neutral sentence describing the item, printed on purchase
quotes    OPTIONAL per-shop dialogue printed after a purchase or sale. Keys are the gear_shop key each shop
sets ('halda', 'halda_sell', 'pawn_sell'); values are full lines and may contain \" quotes.
warn      OPTIONAL [{when, text}]: a ChoiceScript condition and a warning appended to the buy option
tier      armor only: light | medium | heavy (proficiency tier); use 'shield' for shields
sell      { smith: percent, pawn: percent, general: percent, tailor: percent, jeweler: percent, pawnFixed: copper, smithPiece: copper each, herbalistPiece: copper each, countVar: variable }

(a shop's buyer is 'smith', 'pawn', 'general', 'tailor', 'jeweler' or 'herbalist', which buys counted salvage by the piece (herbalistPiece) and nothing else; general is the flat 50 percent counter that Hollis and Vael both use. Each price is floor(retail * pct),
and a price of 0 means that buyer declines, so keep general-goods retail high enough that 50 percent is at least 1)
loadout   slot fields for equipment.txt (weapon, armor and head items; cloak, hands, waist, feet and neck take desc and prose)
traits    OPTIONAL, any worn item: { cold, wet, heat, stat, bonus }. cold, wet and heat are PERCENT CUTS to that part of
outdoor exposure (calendar.txt calc_exposure sums them over every worn slot, capped at 90; a NEGATIVE heat adds
heat wear). stat ('str'..'cha') and bonus add to that ability SCORE while worn. Equipment bonuses to the same
score do NOT stack (only the highest counts) and the Hearthstone counts as one. Generated into equipment.txt
garment_traits; the menu hint text is built from the same numbers. Keep score bonuses to +1 and +2:
a bonus on the d20 roll itself is not for shop gear (see GAMEPLAY_MECHANICS_RULES section 2).
sidearmDesc  weapon items: the description when carried in the sidearm slot
dossier   { line, badgeOn, badgeOff, equipText } for the dossier list and its equip option
inventory { category } for the inventory panel (defaults: weapon weapons, armor/head apparel, tool provisions)
effect    consumable items: { type: 'heal', n, sides, bonus }, { type: 'boon', name, desc, stat, bonus, minutes },
{ type: 'wash' } (resets the hygiene clock to Clean; needs open water within reach, see equipment.txt
water_at_hand, and is refused within 6 hours of the last wash) or
{ type: 'dressing', bonus } (binds a wound: +bonus HP on the next night's sleep that heals, then used up;
refused while unhurt or while a dressing is already on). Add a new type in gen_gear.js effectSummary and
genGearInfo, and in equipment.txt use_consumable.
useVerb   consumables: the verb on the use option ('Drink', 'Rub in')
useText   consumables: the sentence printed when the item is used
combat    consumables: true if it can be used mid-fight (costs the turn)
stack     OPTIONAL true/false: may the player own several copies? Default true for armor, shield, weapon, head and
tool; false for ring and salvage. Copies beyond the first live in spare_<id> (has_<id> stays true while
any copy is owned, so every older has_ check keeps working).
flags     create:false when the has_ flag is created by hand elsewhere; hand:true when the dossier and
inventory entries are written by hand (shield, ring, salvage)
Shops: a shop with "menu": false feeds only the trade panel (no plain menu labels); use it as a union of several category menus.
Trades: `trades` lists the shops that offer the trade panel (web/mygame/trade.js). Each names its scene file, its
label prefix, a buyShop (optional) and a sellShop from `shops`, and the quote keys ('buyKey', 'sellKey') the shop
sets in gear_shop. The generator writes <name>_cart_pass (and <name>_panel_rows for a buy side) and the
trade-data.generated.js the panel reads.

loadout.reach  OPTIONAL, a ranged weapon: how far it shoots, as a reach class (touch | short | medium | long). Default long. A sling is medium (the user, 2026-10-12). Written to weapon_reach / sidearm_reach.

A piece that gives a stat bonus is UNIQUE (the user, 2026-10-13): it cannot be stacked or bought a second time (stack false), and gen_gear.js treats any item with traits.stat that way. Their prices are 400c for +1 and 1,200c to 1,500c for +2: magical dress, not mundane stock.

WEIGHT (2026-10-14, the user asked for a carrying limit): every item has a weight in LOAD points, from 0.1 up (a ring or a gem is 0.1, a longsword 3, plate 14). A character carries 40 + 2 x STR score. Weight is per item: a stack weighs weight x quantity. COINS WEIGH TOO (coin_weights, the user's call, so that turning a hoard into gems, jewelry or notes is a real choice). Starting gear that is not catalog stock is in starting_weights. Not used by any scene yet.

CONTAINERS (2026-10-14, the user's design): a place to put items that is not on the character. Each has an id, a name, a capacity in load points, `needs` (a flag that must be true for it to be reachable, with `needs_reason` as the words when it is not) and `dungeon: "waits"` (it is left outside a dungeon run). Stowed counts are stow_<container>_<item>, created for every pack item the generator makes. A new container is one entry here; the pack reads the list. Kinds in mind: follows you everywhere (a magic bag), follows you but waits outside a dungeon (a horse's saddlebags, a wagon), fixed in a place (a stash).

items.name: hewing axe
items.title: Highland Hewing Axe
items.blurb: A broad-bearded felling axe with the balance forward of the haft.

quotes.halda: "Alderford work," she says. "A river trader brings me a few pieces each season, and the temper on them is honest."

dossier.line: Broad-bearded single-handed felling axe with a hardened wedge
dossier.equipText: Wield the Highland Hewing Axe instead [1d8 Slashing, One-Handed].

items.name: stiletto
items.title: Alderford Stiletto
items.blurb: A slender, square-sided blade ground to a needle point from file-steel.

dossier.line: Slender square-section thrusting dagger ground from scrap file-steel
dossier.equipText: Wield the Alderford Stiletto instead [1d4 Piercing, One-Handed].

items.name: wooden club
items.title: Wooden Club
items.blurb: A length of hardwood, knotted at the head and banded with iron, worn smooth where hands have held it.

dossier.line: Knotted hardwood club with an iron band at the head
dossier.equipText: Wield the Wooden Club instead [1d4 Bludgeoning, One-Handed].

items.name: rough spear
items.title: Rough Spear
items.blurb: A straight ash pole with an iron head bound on with wire and cord.

dossier.line: Straight ash pole with a wired-on iron head
dossier.equipText: Wield the Rough Spear instead [1d6 Piercing, Reach, One-Handed].

items.name: cord sling
items.title: Cord Sling
items.blurb: A braided cord sling with a leather pouch, made for a long throw.

dossier.line: Braided cord and a leather pouch for throwing stones
dossier.equipText: Take up the Cord Sling instead [1d4 Bludgeoning, Ranged, One-Handed].

items.name: hunting bow
items.title: Hunting Bow
items.blurb: A plain yew stave with a waxed string, strung for a day in the woods.

dossier.line: Plain yew stave with a waxed string
dossier.equipText: Take up the Hunting Bow instead [1d6 Piercing, Ranged, Two-Handed].

items.name: iron prybar
items.title: Iron Prybar
items.hint: Advantage on Force and Pry Checks
items.blurb: A three-foot bar of octagonal iron with a curved claw at one end and a chisel heel at the other.

quotes.halda: "Nothing pretty about it," she says. "It opens what someone locked."

dossier.line: Cold-forged crowbar and tempered wedges for forcing stubborn locks and stone seams

items.name: iron skullcap
items.title: Iron Skullcap
items.blurb: A plain riveted iron skullcap with a small touchmark stamped into the brow.

quotes.halda: "It turns a glancing blow," she says.

warn.text: Counts as armor: ends Mage Armor and Unarmored Defense while worn

dossier.line: Plain riveted steel skullcap, guild-stamped at Torvald's forge
dossier.equipText: Wear the Iron Skullcap instead [+1 AC].

dossier.line: Stiffened leather skullcap, cheap and close-fitting under a hood
dossier.equipText: Wear the Leather Watch Cap instead.

items.name: studded gambeson
items.title: Studded Gambeson
items.blurb: A quilted coat with rows of small iron studs sewn between layers of wool and canvas.

quotes.halda: "It'll turn a blow," she says. "It won't turn a bad decision."

dossier.line: Quilted wool-and-canvas coat with rows of iron studs sewn between the layers
dossier.equipText: Wear the Studded Gambeson instead [Medium Armor: AC 13 + DEX, max +2].

items.name: mail shirt
items.title: Iron Chain Shirt
items.blurb: Every link is closed by hand, and the seams at the neck and hips are doubled.

quotes.halda: "Rings are honest," she says. "I checked every one."

dossier.line: Hand-closed mail rings over a wool lining, with doubled seams at the neck and hips
dossier.equipText: Wear the Iron Chain Shirt instead [Medium Armor: AC 13 + DEX, max +2].

items.name: iron plate harness
items.title: Iron Plate Harness
items.hint: Heavy Armor: AC 16, no DEX bonus
items.blurb: Overlapping iron plates over a mail coat, the shoulders hinged and the hip plates lapped like roof tiles.

quotes.halda: "Good for a bad day," she says. "Bad for a long walk."

dossier.line: Overlapping iron plates riveted over a mail coat, with hinged shoulders and lapped hip plates
dossier.equipText: Wear the Iron Plate Harness instead [Heavy Armor: AC 16, no DEX bonus].

items.name: oak shield
items.title: Oak Shield
items.blurb: A round oak shield with an iron boss, oak from the valley and iron from the harbor wagons.

quotes.halda: "It'll take a hit that would break a wrist," she says.

items.name: warming liniment
items.title: Warming Liniment
items.blurb: A thumb-length of grey camphor-and-thyme tallow twisted in waxed paper.

quotes.ambrose: Master Ambrose shows you where to rub it in: wrists, knees, the small of the back, while it is still warm.

items.useText: You work the grey tallow into your wrists and knees. It smells of camphor and thyme, and it warms them within a few breaths. The stiffness goes out.

dossier.line: Pot of grey camphor-and-thyme tallow for stiff joints

items.name: clear-head draught
items.title: Clear-Head Draught
items.blurb: A stoppered measure of amber liquid, pine and mint with something bitter underneath.

quotes.ambrose: Master Ambrose corks the bottle and tells you to drink it whole, not sip it.

items.useText: You drink the amber liquid: pine and mint, with something bitter underneath. It burns going down and leaves your head cool and quiet.

dossier.line: Corked bottle of amber pine-and-mint tonic

items.name: phial of Saint Althea's water
items.title: Saint Althea's Water
items.blurb: A wax-stoppered clay flask of blessed cistern-water steeped with wild angelica and mountain arnica.
items.useText: You wrench the wax stopper free and swallow the cold, herbal draught. Radiant warmth floods through you, knitting torn muscle and staunching fresh bleeding.

dossier.line: Wax-stoppered clay flask of blessed cistern-water steeped with wild angelica and mountain arnica

items.name: linen bandage
items.title: Linen Bandage
items.blurb: A clean strip of boiled linen, rolled tight around a pad of comfrey leaf and tied off with thread.

quotes.ambrose: "Boiled, then dried in the sun," Master Ambrose says. "Clean linen does half the work. Bind it snug and leave it be until morning."

items.useText: You bind the linen over your worst wound, snug enough to hold the comfrey pad in place and loose enough to let the blood move. It will stay on until you have slept.

dossier.line: Boiled linen rolled around a pad of comfrey leaf, for binding a wound before sleep

items.name: lye soap
items.title: Lye Soap
items.hint: Hygiene back to Clean, with water at hand
items.blurb: A twist of brown paper holding grey shavings of lye soap, enough for one good scrub.

quotes.hollis: "Grey soap, honest lye," Hollis says. "You bring the water. A stream will do, or the shore. It'll take the skin off a bad conscience."

items.useText: You crouch at the water's edge, tip the shavings into your palm, and work up a stinging grey lather. You scrub your hands, neck and face with it and rinse in the water, and the road comes away in streaks.

dossier.line: Brown-paper twist of grey lye-soap shavings, enough for one wash by a stream or the shore

items.name: trail rations
items.title: Trail Rations
items.hint: Eaten for you on the road when you grow hungry
items.blurb: A day's food wrapped in a cloth: a hard biscuit, a stick of dried sausage, and a fist of raisins.

quotes.hollis: "One a day is enough to walk on," Hollis says. "You'll tire of it by the second. You'll still eat it."

items.useText: You unwrap the cloth and eat the biscuit, the sausage and the raisins, one after the other. It is plain food, and it is enough.

dossier.line: Cloth-wrapped biscuit, dried sausage and raisins, a day's food on the road

items.name: hemp rope
items.title: Hemp Rope
items.blurb: Fifty feet of tarred hemp as thick as a thumb, coiled tight and tied off with a slip-knot.

quotes.hollis: "Tarred, so a wet cellar won't rot it," Hollis says. "Test it before you trust it. I do."

dossier.line: Fifty feet of tarred hemp rope, coiled and tied off

items.name: torch
items.title: Torch
items.blurb: A pine stave bound with tarred rag and dipped in pitch, good for about an hour of steady light.

dossier.line: Pine stave wrapped in tarred rag and dipped in pitch

items.name: lamp oil
items.title: Lamp Oil
items.blurb: A stoppered tin flask of lamp oil, enough to keep a lantern burning through a long night.

dossier.line: Stoppered tin flask of lamp oil

items.name: hooded lantern
items.title: Hooded Lantern
items.blurb: An iron lantern with horn windows and a sliding tin shutter, its oil pot filled through a hinged cap on top.

quotes.hollis: "Same as the ones over the doors, only this one goes where you go," Hollis says. "Slide the shutter across and nobody sees the flame."

dossier.line: Iron lantern with horn windows and a sliding tin shutter

items.name: repair kit
items.title: Repair Kit
items.blurb: A canvas roll holding a claw hammer, chisel, awl, pliers, folding saw, and soft wire for field repairs and simple mechanisms.

quotes.hollis: "Nothing fancy," Hollis says. "Anything that can be mended with a hammer and some patience, that roll will mend."

dossier.line: Canvas roll of repair tools for field fixes and simple mechanisms

items.name: shovel
items.title: Shovel
items.blurb: A long-handled shovel with a flat iron blade, its handle worn smooth by someone else's hands.

dossier.line: Long-handled iron shovel for digging

items.name: lute
items.title: Lute
items.blurb: A pear-bellied lute of plain maple with seven gut strings, a worn pick-guard, and one tuning peg replaced in a different wood.

quotes.hollis: "Came in with a sailor who needed supper more than a song," Hollis says. "The belly's sound and the strings are new. Tune it before you play, and again after."

dossier.line: Plain maple lute with seven gut strings and a worn pick-guard

items.name: flint and tinderbox
items.title: Flint and Tinderbox
items.blurb: A dented tin box holding a striker, a lump of flint, and a wad of char-cloth that catches from a single spark.

dossier.line: Dented tin box with a striker, flint and dry char-cloth

items.name: chalk sticks
items.title: Chalk Sticks
items.hint: Six chalk marks for a dungeon map
items.blurb: Six sticks of soft white chalk tied together with string, for marking a wall or a route.

quotes.hollis: "Same chalk that's on my slate," Hollis says, and taps the stub hanging from his apron. "Mark your turns. It's the one thing in a tunnel that doesn't lie to you."

dossier.line: Six sticks of soft white chalk tied with string

items.name: camp kit
items.title: Camp Kit
items.hint: +1 HP sleeping rough; the tent keeps rain off at camp
items.blurb: A canvas tent with its poles and pegs rolled inside a wool bedroll, with a bone needle and waxed thread tucked in the fold, all tied with cord.

dossier.line: Canvas tent, poles and pegs rolled in a wool bedroll, with needle and thread

items.name: oilcloth sheet
items.title: Oilcloth Sheet
items.hint: Halves the wear of rain and storms on the road
items.blurb: A square of canvas soaked in linseed oil and wax, stiff as a board when cold, that sheds rain like a roof.

quotes.hollis: "Drape it over your pack or over your head," Hollis says. "Rain runs off it and you stay dry underneath."

dossier.line: Square of canvas soaked in linseed oil and wax, stiff and rain-proof

items.name: lockpick set
items.title: Lockpick Set
items.blurb: A leather roll holding a dozen slim steel picks, two tension wrenches, and a hooked rake, each in its own loop.

quotes.vael: "Every pick I sell shows me where the next lock has to be stronger," Vael says. "So I sell them."

dossier.line: Leather roll of slim steel picks, tension wrenches and a hooked rake

items.name: padlock and key
items.title: Padlock and Key
items.blurb: A heavy brass padlock with a hardened steel shackle, hung on a loop of cord with its two keys.

quotes.vael: "Forged here, not bought in," Vael says. "Two keys. Lose one and the sign over my counter says what a new one costs."

dossier.line: Heavy brass padlock with a steel shackle and two keys

items.name: door bolt
items.title: Door Bolt
items.blurb: A forged iron slide-bolt with its keeper plate and four wood screws wrapped in cloth, small enough to carry in a pack.

quotes.vael: "Screw it to any door and it holds against a shoulder," Vael says. "Against a wedge, ask me for something bigger."

dossier.line: Forged iron slide-bolt with a keeper plate and wood screws

items.name: iron manacles
items.title: Iron Manacles
items.blurb: A pair of hinged iron cuffs joined by a short chain, with a single key on a ring.

quotes.vael: "Hinged, keyed, and heavier than they look," Vael says. "I don't ask who goes in them."

dossier.line: Pair of hinged iron cuffs on a short chain, with one key

items.name: traveler's cloak
items.title: Traveler's Cloak
items.blurb: A full-length cloak of stout undyed broadcloth, cut wide enough to close over a pack, with a double-stitched hem.

quotes.tailor: "Broadcloth," Fenwick says. "It has no opinions about fashion, and it keeps its shape in the rain."

dossier.line: Full-length cloak of stout undyed broadcloth
dossier.equipText: Wear the Traveler's Cloak instead.

items.name: storm cape
items.title: Storm Cape
items.blurb: A short cape of canvas-backed wool, rubbed with beeswax until water beads and rolls off it.

quotes.tailor: "Waxed twice and left to cure," Fenwick says. "The wax is what does the work, so keep it away from the fire."

dossier.line: Short waxed cape that sheds rain like a slate roof
dossier.equipText: Wear the Storm Cape instead.

items.name: winter cloak
items.title: Winter Cloak
items.blurb: A heavy grey cloak lined edge to edge in marten fur, with a collar that stands up past the ears.

quotes.tailor: "In January you will think of me kindly," Fenwick says. "In August you will think of me less kindly. Own something lighter as well."

dossier.line: Heavy grey cloak lined in marten fur, with a tall collar
dossier.equipText: Wear the Winter Cloak instead.

items.name: summer duster
items.title: Summer Duster
items.blurb: A loose, ankle-length coat of bleached linen with wide sleeves and a back vent that lets the air through.

quotes.tailor: "Linen is cooler than the sun," Fenwick says. "Not by much, but by enough to matter on the road."

dossier.line: Loose ankle-length linen coat with a vented back
dossier.equipText: Wear the Summer Duster instead.

items.name: felt hat
items.title: Felt Hat
items.blurb: A pressed grey felt hat with a broad brim and a grosgrain band, the crown blocked to hold its shape.

dossier.line: Pressed grey felt hat with a broad brim
dossier.equipText: Wear the Felt Hat instead.

items.name: fur cap
items.title: Fur Cap
items.blurb: A close wool cap with turn-down flaps trimmed in rabbit fur, tied under the chin with a leather lace.

dossier.line: Close wool cap with fur-trimmed flaps
dossier.equipText: Wear the Fur Cap instead.

items.name: pair of lined gloves
items.title: Lined Gloves
items.blurb: Supple leather gloves lined with combed fleece, with a long cuff that tucks under a sleeve.

dossier.line: Soft leather gloves lined with combed fleece
dossier.equipText: Wear the Lined Gloves instead.

items.name: pair of lamplight gloves
items.title: Lamplight Gloves
items.blurb: Fine black kid gloves, cut close across the knuckles so a quill or a page can be worked without taking them off. The fingertips warm a little when they rest on a lit page.

quotes.tailor: "For people who read for a living," Fenwick says. "The fit is in the knuckle. Everything else is decoration."
quotes.tailor_sell: Fenwick draws the gloves off the paper one finger at a time and looks at the seams against the skylight. "The finishing is in the thread," he says. "It has to be unpicked before I can sell them again."

dossier.line: Fine black kid gloves cut close for close work
dossier.equipText: Wear the Lamplight Gloves instead.

items.name: pair of spellseeker gloves
items.title: Spellseeker Gloves
items.blurb: Black kid gloves cut from a single skin, each finger fitted to a plaster cast of the hand, and stitched in silk. The stitching is doubled in pale thread along every finger, and the fingertips warm whenever they pass near a written line.

quotes.tailor: "I measure each finger twice," Fenwick says. "You will not thank me for it, but you will not think about them again either, and that is the point."
quotes.tailor_sell: Fenwick lays the gloves on the brown paper and does not touch them for a moment. "A great deal of thread in those," he says. "It all comes out before another hand goes in, and that is days of work. Hence the figure."

dossier.line: Black kid gloves fitted finger by finger and stitched in silk
dossier.equipText: Wear the Spellseeker Gloves instead.

items.name: pair of rain boots
items.title: Rain Boots
items.blurb: Knee-high boots of oiled calf with a stitched welt, the seams waxed shut and the tops cut to shed a rain-soaked cloak.

quotes.tailor: "Waxed seams, sewn welt," Fenwick says. "They will outlast the horse."

dossier.line: Knee-high oiled calf boots with waxed seams
dossier.equipText: Wear the Rain Boots instead.

items.name: pair of winter boots
items.title: Winter Boots
items.blurb: Thick-soled boots of stiff leather lined with pressed felt, laced high with a snow-cuff of wool.

dossier.line: Thick-soled boots lined with pressed felt
dossier.equipText: Wear the Winter Boots instead.

items.name: pair of swallowstep shoes
items.title: Swallowstep Shoes
items.blurb: Flat black shoes of soft kid with a thin, flexible sole and a strap over the instep, made for a ballroom floor. A second line of pale stitching runs along the strap, and the sole seems to rise to meet the floor.

quotes.tailor: "The sole is thin on purpose," Fenwick says. "You will feel the floor, and so will your feet. It is not a road shoe."
quotes.tailor_sell: Fenwick turns the shoes over, finds the pale stitching along the strap with a fingernail, and starts to unpick it. "The finishing has to come out before they go back on the stool," he says. "That is what the forty in the hundred is for."

dossier.line: Flat black kid shoes with a thin flexible sole
dossier.equipText: Wear the Swallowstep Shoes instead.

items.name: wool muffler
items.title: Wool Muffler
items.blurb: A long knitted muffler of thick grey wool, wound twice about the neck and tucked into the collar.

dossier.line: Long knitted grey wool muffler
dossier.equipText: Wear the Wool Muffler instead.

items.name: silvertongue cravat
items.title: Silvertongue Cravat
items.blurb: A neckcloth of dove-grey silk, folded and pinned in the Quarter fashion so the knot sits under the chin. Once pinned, the folds settle on their own and stay where they fell.

quotes.tailor: "The knot is the whole trick," Fenwick says, and folds it for you once, quickly, so you can see how.
quotes.tailor_sell: Fenwick shakes the neckcloth out and the folds hold their shape for a moment too long. "Finished for one throat," he says. "I will have to take the second stitch out before anyone else wears it."

dossier.line: Dove-grey silk neckcloth folded in the Quarter fashion
dossier.equipText: Wear the Silvertongue Cravat instead.

items.name: envoy's court coat
items.title: Envoy's Court Coat
items.blurb: A long-skirted coat in charcoal wool with a silk lining, cut close through the shoulder and finished with covered buttons. It hangs the same on every wearer, and people nearby stand a little straighter without knowing why.

quotes.tailor: "Cut to you, not to a peg," Fenwick says. "It is not armor. It is the reason a door opens."
quotes.tailor_sell: Fenwick runs a thumb along the lapel and shakes his head slowly. "Finished for you. I will have to unpick the second stitch before it can hang for anyone else, and that costs me."

dossier.line: Charcoal wool coat, silk-lined and cut close through the shoulder
dossier.equipText: Wear the Envoy's Court Coat instead [Cloth armor: AC 10 + DEX; +2 CHA].

items.hint: Cloth armor: AC 10 + DEX; cold -25%, rain -10%; +2 CHA

warn.text: Replaces the armor you are wearing

items.name: ash quarterstaff
items.title: Ash Quarterstaff
items.blurb: A six-foot staff of straight-grained Longshade ash, planed round and rubbed with linseed until it shines.

dossier.line: Six-foot staff of straight-grained Longshade ash, planed round and oiled
dossier.equipText: Wield the Ash Quarterstaff instead [1d6 Bludgeoning, One-Handed].

items.name: Longshade spear
items.title: Longshade Spear
items.blurb: A seven-foot ash shaft with a leaf-bladed iron head pinned through a socket, the grain running true from butt to point.

dossier.line: Seven-foot Longshade ash shaft with a leaf-bladed iron head
dossier.equipText: Wield the Longshade Spear instead [1d6 Piercing, Reach, One-Handed].

items.name: Longshade shortbow
items.title: Longshade Shortbow

starting_weights._note: Load weights for gear the game hands out by name instead of as catalog stock (equipment.txt grant_class_armor, grant_class_weapons, origin_clothing). The same unit as an item weight. armor is keyed by starting_armor, weapons by starting_weapon, sidearms by the class's sidearm id (sidearm_by_class), clothing is every character's four plain pieces.

coin_weights._note: Load weight of ONE coin of each kind (the purse is always held as the fewest coins: 10 copper = 1 silver mark, 10 silver = 1 gold crown, see economy.txt currency_add), so a purse weighs gold x 0.25 + silver x 0.1 + copper x 0.05. A gem, a piece of jewelry or (later) a note of credit carries the same value for far less load. The Gilded Scales Letter of Credit (the account the factors' halls and the Port Valen head house keep, has_letter_of_credit and letter_of_credit_value in startup.txt) is one sealed paper: 0.1 while there is a balance, whatever the sum.

capacity._note: What a character can carry on their own back: base + per_str x the STR score (the user doubled the first draft, 2026-10-14). That is the one capacity everywhere: the Load bar, the shop warnings and the penalty all use it. Over it, every point over adds over_pct_per_point percent (rounded up, so any excess costs something) to how fast the rest clock runs while MOVING (overworld legs and dungeon steps, never sleeping), up to over_pct_cap. `horse` is 0 on purpose (the user's call, 2026-10-14): a horse's capacity must not inflate the character's own, because it is not with them in a dungeon. It is reserved for the saddlebags, a separate container with explicit stow and take-back, planned with other containers (a wagon, a stash in a fixed place).

containers.name: Saddlebags
containers.needs_reason: Your horse is not with you.
containers.note: Carried by your horse. It never counts toward your own load, and it waits outside when you go into a dungeon.
